result.title: Attention Latent Feedback
result.summary: During autoregressive decoding, the deeper representations of the previous token have already been computed, yet shallow layers at the current token cannot read them directly because standard self-attention connects positions only at the same depth. We introduce Attention Latent Feedback (ALF), an architecture that allows every sublayer to attend to the outputs of the deeper layers at the previous position. Training unrolls this cross-position recurrence into two parallel passes, whereas decoding remains single-pass using cached previous-token states. Across mixture-of-experts models with up to 4.0B parameters, ALF lowers held-out loss by 0.022-0.024 nats over the standard residual with about 1.1% decoding FLOP overhead, and consistently outperforms prior final-state feedback across all three scales on both standard and attention residual backbones. On MoE-1.6B, ALF matches a $1.38\times$ larger baseline token budget, and on MoE-4.0B it lifts average accuracy across seventeen downstream benchmarks from 45.1% to 47.0%. Analysis further reveals that intermediate and nearby deeper layers drive most of this benefit, allowing a fixed nearest-window variant to retain 89%-94% of the gain at linear read cost while learned attention widens its margin with scale.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Attention Latent Feedback（ALF）架构：自回归解码时让每个子层注意上一位置深层层的输出，训练时把跨位置递推展开为两遍并行计算，解码仍单遍并复用缓存的上一 token 状态；在最大 4.0B 的 MoE 模型上降低 held-out loss 并提升十七项下游基准平均准确率，同时分析有效的深层窗口。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本架构，不直接研究视觉推理，但「深层 latent 反馈给浅层、跨位置状态回传、缓存复用与有效深度窗口」可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态如何回注与深度/位置选取，可能为 latent 反馈训练和状态复用提供线索。
